Pete Bagnall on the second stage held on to this position behind Eastleigh, St. Albans and Finchley, Eastleigh having surprisingly maintained their lead given to them by their very promising performer Dobson.
On turning into Cambridge Road, Dave Baulch and Pete Bagnall pulled away slightly from Charlie Walker and these three were then some forty yards ahead of Davidson, Flanagan and Bishop.
Pete Bagnall set out from Old Palace Yard, Westminster, on the first stroke of ten by Big Ben. Just before Chelsea Bridge, Ian Boyd running for Herne Hill, jumped the field and began to draw away.

Pete Bagnall and Len Bishop were 1st and 2nd in the three miles and it was good to see Len out again after an injury. The senior 4 x 440 yards relay of Sexton, Glen, Boreham and Heathfield, won despite good opposition and having already competed during the afternoon in other races.

Len Bishop,in place of our regular first runner,P.Bagnall, who was injured,rose well above the form he had shown of late, giving us a reasonably good start finishing 6th behind Poly,H.H.H Aylesford, Hampstead,and St.Albans in that order.

Walker, Pete Bagnall, Dave Baulch and Eric Gebbett, all running strongly and all four within reach of one another but unable apparently to join forces, a fact which probably cost us second team place.

The finish saw Jack in 11th place, with Gebbett our next man home 114th, Dave Baulch 141st, Ray Tooby, who had manfully stood up to a course for which he was not physically suited 147th, whilst Chas Walker held on to finish 173rd from Len Bishop 181st.
